record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: When secure aggregation is used for privacy in federated learning, how can systems still defend against adversarial attacks, develop efficient range proofs, and determine which nonlinear or Byzantine-robust aggregation methods can be computed efficiently under secure aggregation?

evidence.quote: how to defend against adversarial attacks when secure aggregation is used

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning system in which $n$ clients hold local model updates $x_1, \dots, x_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a central server wishes to learn only the aggregate $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ (or some function thereof) under a cryptographic secure aggregation protocol that hides every individual $x_i$ from the server and from other clients. Within this setting, address the following three problems:

(a) Adversarial robustness under secure aggregation. Design a protocol that defends against adversarial clients who submit arbitrarily corrupted updates $x_i$ aimed at degrading model accuracy or implanting backdoors, while preserving the privacy guarantee that no individual $x_i$ is revealed. Specify a threat model (e.g., up to a fraction $\beta < 1$ of malicious clients with full knowledge of the protocol), and prove correctness and privacy guarantees for the proposed defense.

(b) Efficient range proofs. Construct a cryptographic protocol that allows each client to prove, in zero knowledge to the server (or to a set of verifiers), that its encrypted contribution $x_i$ lies within a prescribed set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ (for example, that $\|x_i\|_p \le B$ for given $p$ and bound $B$), such that the per-client communication and computation, and the server's verification cost, are sublinear or otherwise practically efficient in $d$ and in $n$. Quantify the achievable trade-offs between proof size, soundness error, and computational cost.

(c) Nonlinear and Byzantine-robust aggregation under secure aggregation. Characterize which aggregation functions $f(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ — in particular nonlinear robust aggregators such as coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, geometric median, Krum, or Multi-Krum — can be computed under a secure aggregation protocol with communication and computation cost polynomial in $n$ and $d$ and with cryptographic privacy guarantees matching those of linear secure aggregation. For each such function, provide an explicit protocol with complexity bounds; for functions shown not to admit such efficient protocols, prove a corresponding lower bound or impossibility result.
artifact.status_search_result: Active research has produced partial solutions: frameworks such as ByzSFL, RiseFL, and PriRoAgg combine zero-knowledge proofs, hybrid commitments, and Lagrange-coded computing to provide Byzantine-robust secure aggregation and bounded-norm range proofs, while earlier work (e.g., Prio's SNIP, and "Secure Byzantine-Robust Machine Learning") gives limited input validation. However, no single approach achieves efficient secure aggregation simultaneously for arbitrary nonlinear robust aggregators with tight complexity bounds, and the general characterization of which robust aggregators admit efficient secure computation remains open.

status_evidence.title: ByzSFL: Achieving Byzantine-Robust Secure Federated Learning with Zero-Knowledge Proofs
status_evidence.snippet: ByzSFL is an efficient Byzantine-robust secure aggregation framework that incorporates a ZKP protocol toolkit enabling clients to prove validity of aggregation weight computations without revealing sensitive information.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: ZKP-based Byzantine-robust secure aggregation is feasible.

status_evidence.title: PriRoAgg: Achieving Robust Model Aggregation with Minimum Privacy Leakage
status_evidence.snippet: PriRoAgg utilizes Lagrange coded computing and distributed zero-knowledge proofs to execute a wide range of robust aggregation algorithms while satisfying aggregated privacy.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple robust aggregators can be executed under privacy constraints, but full characterization remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Robust and Secure Federated Learning with Low-Cost Zero-Knowledge Proof (RiseFL)
status_evidence.snippet: RiseFL proposes a hybrid commitment scheme and probabilistic input integrity check method supporting Byzantine-robust aggregation.
status_evidence.claim: Efficient probabilistic range/integrity checks are achievable, addressing part (b).

status_evidence.title: Secure Byzantine-Robust Machine Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Studies combining secure aggregation with Byzantine robustness, noting that existing methods provide only limited input validation such as norm range checks.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work indicates the combined problem is only partially addressed.
